title: Geometric predicates for adic formal completions
statement: For an adic formal completion presentation $C=(X,I)$ [def-per-adic-formal-completion], define the absolute singular ideal of a ring $A$ to be the vanishing ideal of the primes where $A_{\mathfrak p}$ is not regular local [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Define the reduced singular ideal of $X$ as the vanishing ideal of the closure of its nonregular points (the closure is redundant when this locus is closed). For a small-singular-locus pair [def-per-small-singular-locus-pair], its completion presentation is its scheme and divisor ideal. The completion is reduced and quasi-excellent if every Noetherian complete formal affine chart has reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme] and quasi-excellent [def-exc-excellent-ring] coordinate ring. Its extended ideal of definition is invertible if on every original completed affine chart it is finitely generated and the ring is complete for its powers, and on a finite affine cover of $X$ the extended ideals are generated by non-zero-divisors [def-nagata-invertible-ideal]. It is a finite disjoint union of characteristic-zero formal varieties if there is a finite clopen partition of the formal space into pieces isomorphic to Noetherian formal completion presentations whose reduced closed fibres have finite-type structure maps to spectra of characteristic-zero fields [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]; the fields may differ. It has completed singular locus when on every completed affine chart its absolute singular ideal equals the extension of the reduced singular ideal of $X$; the completed closed subspace is then the completion of this reduced singular subscheme, with thickening rings $B/(J+I^n)$. It is rig-regular when on every completed affine chart some positive power of the ideal of definition lies in the absolute singular ideal. The empty clopen partition is allowed.

source.place: Temkin, Non-embedded desingularization, §§2.4.1,2.4.3,2.4.9,2.4.11 and §§3.1.1,3.1.4; construction used in the proof of Theorem 3.4.1, printed p.26.
